label: Person
name: Ray Johnson
summary:
Raymond Edward "Ray" Johnson was an American artist. Known primarily as a collagist and correspondence artist, he was a seminal figure in the history of Neo-Dada and early Pop art and was described as "New York's most famous unknown artist". Johnson also staged and participated in early performance art events as the founder of a far-ranging mail art network – the New York Correspondence School – which picked up momentum in the 1960s and is still active today.

He is occasionally associated with members of the Fluxus movement but was never a member. Ray Johnson was a painters & sculptors from Detroit (1927-10-16, Detroit–1995-01-13). A moderately significant entity in the historical record. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a key figure in Neo-Dada and early Pop art, Ray Johnson's work influenced the development of mail art and performance art, contributing to a cultural shift in the 1960s. His network, the New York Correspondence School, continues to operate today.
